items.title: Forward additional signals to the child process in `uv run`
items.reason: The merged diff added SIGPIPE registration and unconditional forwarding to the child, matching the source-backed part of this report. It originally fixed the opposite problem of signals not reaching children.

items.title: Unexpected behavior when handling signals
items.reason: This bug was closed by astral-sh/uv#13017. It concerned orphaned children when externally delivered signals were not forwarded, rather than uv-generated SIGPIPE killing a child.

items.title: Handling of signal exit from subprocess is incorrect
items.reason: This tracks how `uv run` maps a signal-terminated child to 128+signal without preserving the shell-visible diagnostic. It explains status 141 after SIGPIPE but not the unintended forwarding.

related.search_scope: No exact existing tracker was found. Literal searches covered SIGPIPE, EPIPE, writev, broken pipe, exit code 141/status 141/signal 13, HTTP/2 timeout, and network-triggered `uv run` termination. Conceptual searches covered Unix signal forwarding, child processes, process groups, and Tokio signal handling. Fix-oriented searches covered closed issues and pull requests, particularly astral-sh/uv#13017 and astral-sh/uv#12830. astral-sh/uv#12244 was ruled out because it concerns shell-completion output writing to a closed stdout pipe and uv panicking, not network SIGPIPE forwarded to a child. astral-sh/uv#3095 is a broader exec design discussion, not a tracker for this failure.

type_reason: The Unix child runner registers a SIGPIPE listener and unconditionally sends every received SIGPIPE to the spawned child. astral-sh/uv#13017 introduced this while addressing externally delivered signals, but forwarding an incidental signal generated by uv's own I/O can incorrectly terminate an unrelated child. The reported HTTP/2 timeout/writev origin remains unconfirmed. No open issue or pull request tracks this specific failure, so it is a bug rather than a duplicate.
summary: No exact duplicate was found. astral-sh/uv#13017 introduced the relevant SIGPIPE forwarding while fixing astral-sh/uv#12830; astral-sh/uv#11886 separately explains why a SIGPIPE-killed child appears as exit 141.
draft_response: Thanks for the report and reproducer. The current Unix child runner registers a SIGPIPE handler and unconditionally forwards received SIGPIPE signals to the spawned command; that behavior was added in astral-sh/uv#13017 while fixing a different signal-forwarding problem. This supports treating the child termination as a uv bug. We have not independently confirmed that the signal originates from the reported HTTP/2 timeout/writev path. Could you capture a failing `uv -vv run --frozen -m modulename` invocation and confirm whether `Received SIGPIPE, forwarding to child` appears immediately before the exit? The next implementation step is to reproduce this against current main and add regression coverage ensuring uv's own incidental SIGPIPE is not delivered to the child.
